phase2.rebuttals: Read 19abf1c's todo.md record and checked its claims instead of its framing. (1) The rebuttal of round 1's repro holds -- I ran that repro on 19abf1c myself: still red, output 'first send after 0.00s, gap between greeting and buttons 1.04s, turn 1.04s' (round 1: turn 3.06s). send_times[0] is the typing indicator (send_typing_indicator goes through send_raw), so the measured 'gap' is indicator -> greeting, i.e. the one 1s connect timeout paid by the first enqueue (customer_message) before the breaker trips. The second assertion (total < 1.5) now passes. Rejecting the evidence form while fixing the problem is correct per REVIEW.md lesson 2, and the replacement wiring test excludes the indicator explicitly. (2) 'One second per 30s, same as user_store pays on the same Redis; zero would need a memory queue + writer thread, i.e. redesigning 40.1' -- agreed; my e2e_redis_down rerun shows 1.02s on the first turn and 0.02s on the next two. (3) Self-decisions 1-5 (receipt occurred_at from Meta, switch-off returns before any work, profile-less reply uses `to`, [unknown]/[list_reply] fallbacks, handover occurred_at = enqueue time) all hold; 5 is safe against the contract's 'older occurred_at ignored' rule because the comparison is strict and events from one process are delivered in order. (4) 'Suite 1210 passed with CRM env' matches my 1208 passed + 2 known env failures. One thing the record leaves unsaid rather than wrong: the breaker turns a single transient Redis error (e.g. one 1s operation timeout while Redis is otherwise up) into 30s of dropped events for every visitor, including handover_changed -- previously one event. It is the deliberate user_store trade-off, the commit message states the drop, and CRM display falls back to expires_at; I did not report it, but it is a behaviour change the todo describes only for the 'Redis down' case.
phase2.blind_spot: Its 'known, not handled' list: gateway path pushing customer_message (accepted at batch level), near-simultaneous messages not ordered (accepted edge case), and outbound `recipient` for BSUID visitors unverified against Meta. I covered the last only as an e2e 'not verified' line, and like round 1 my rerun used round 1's stub Meta and status payloads, which were written from the same assumptions as the code -- so the Meta boundary (recipient vs to, recipient_user_id on statuses) remains verified by nobody, me included. The other blind spot is procedural: I leaned on round 1's harness rather than building an independent one, so anything round 1's scenario does not walk (e.g. image/document turns through the real send loop, timed notify pushes with real timers) I verified only by reading plus the unit tests.
